quantity.quote: The PICO Collaboration (formed from the merger of PICASSO and COUPP) has now operated a 2.90 kg C3 F8 bubble chamber from October 2013 to May 2014 in the SNOLAB underground laboratory in Canada, at 6010 meters of water equivalent depth.

New data are reported from the operation of a 2-liter C$_3$F$_8$ bubble chamber in the 2100 meter deep SNOLAB underground laboratory, with a total exposure of 211.5 kg-days at four different recoil energy thresholds ranging from 3.2 keV to 8.1 keV.
New data are reported from a second run of the 2-liter PICO-2L C$_3$F$_8$ bubble chamber with a total exposure of 129$\,$kg-days at a thermodynamic threshold energy of 3.3$\,$keV.

The PICO Collaboration (formed from the merger of PICASSO and COUPP) has now operated a 2.90 kg C3 F8 bubble chamber from October 2013 to May 2014 in the SNOLAB underground laboratory in Canada, at 6010 meters of water equivalent depth.

Result records cover the two published runs (Phys. Rev. Lett. 114, 231302 and Phys. Rev. D 93, 061101); 1905.12522 (electron-recoil nucleation model) also uses PICO-2L calibration data.

summary.plain: PICO-2L was the first bubble chamber installed at SNOLAB by the PICO team: two litres of superheated C3F8 refrigerant. It showed that such chambers can reach low energy thresholds and set strong limits on dark matter that couples to nuclear spin.
summary.technical: 2-litre (2.90 kg) superheated C3F8 chamber at SNOLAB (6010 m.w.e.): run 1 October 2013-May 2014 (211.5 kg-days, 3.2-8.1 keV thresholds; anomalous background events), run 2 February-November 2015 (129 kg-days at 3.3 keV, with particulate contamination controlled: one single-recoil candidate). Reused COUPP-4kg's location, shield and jar design.
